B-1.why: S-1, Internet access: Form 470 certified 5 January, Allowable Contract Date 2 February, so it can be filed today. Brightmarrow's 16,800 dollar bid is lower but Brightmarrow drafted the Form 470 (BD-2, LE-1) and cannot bid; of the other two, Tallis's 18,000 dollars is lower than Northgate's 21,000. 80 percent of 18,000 dollars is 14,400. File inside the window, which closes Wednesday 1 April 2026

B-4.why: S-2, managed Wi-Fi: Form 470 certified 9 January, Allowable Contract Date 6 February; Northgate's 17,500 dollars is lower than Tallis's 19,200. 80 percent of 17,500 dollars is 14,000. File inside the window, which closes Wednesday 1 April 2026

B-6.why: S-3, network switches: Form 470 certified 14 January, Allowable Contract Date 11 February; the lowest bid, Dunmere's 12,000 dollars, arrived only by post (D-1, logged in BD-3 as B-6) and is not on the portal; the portal bids are 13,900 and 14,600. 80 percent of 12,000 dollars is 9,600. File inside the window, which closes Wednesday 1 April 2026

B-13.why: S-8, the fiber link: Form 470 certified 12 January, Allowable Contract Date 9 February; Tallis's 7,000 dollars is lower than Northgate's 8,200. 80 percent of 7,000 dollars is 5,600. File inside the window, which closes Wednesday 1 April 2026

traps.B-2: Brightmarrow's solutions engineer drafted the Form 470 for S-1 and is its named contact (BD-2, and the 1,500 dollar invoice LE-1): a vendor that prepared the Form 470 makes the competition not fair and open, and policy BD-1 bars its bid, though its price is the lowest
traps.B-3: Northgate's 21,000 dollars for S-1 is the highest of the eligible bids: price is the primary factor and Tallis's 18,000 is lower
traps.B-5: Tallis's 19,200 dollars for S-2 is higher than Northgate's 17,500: price is the primary factor
traps.B-7: Northgate's 13,900 dollars for S-3 is the lowest bid on the portal, and not the lowest bid: Dunmere's mailed 12,000 dollars is lower
traps.B-8: Tallis's 14,600 dollars for S-3 is the highest of the three bids for the switches
traps.B-9: S-4, the firewall service: its Form 470 was certified on 2 February, so its Allowable Contract Date is 2 March 2026, 11 days from now; a Form 471 before then commits the district before the 28 days
traps.B-10: S-5, Wi-Fi hotspots for the school buses, is off-campus use: the FCC made school-bus Wi-Fi and off-premises hotspots ineligible (FCC 25-63, FCC 25-62) and the Eligible Services List leaves off-campus use out
traps.B-11: S-6, 300 student Chromebooks, are end-user devices: the Eligible Services List names computers, laptops and tablets as ineligible
traps.B-12: S-7, basic maintenance of internal connections, already has a certified Form 471 (application 261044812, 28 January 2026): a second one would duplicate it
traps.B-14: Northgate's 8,200 dollars for S-8 is higher than Tallis's 7,000: price is the primary factor

traps.M-1: A consultant that takes 12 percent of the funding committed for filing forms the technology director can file free, which the district's policy gives to the director; a reply that says yes commits a share of the funding
traps.M-2: A vendor's offer of a 100 dollar gift card for confirming it: gifts from a provider are limited to 50 dollars per funding year (54.503(d)), and confirming a vendor by reply is no selection under the price-first rule
